meta.changelog: v3 (26 Sep): Captain's Voice (owner-chosen per-role command keys) replaces the horn; building levels and home tiers are checklist-recognised (plaque scan), never blueprint-bound; new lanes: Builder (builders_hut, defense_plans, masonry), battle roles (spearmen, longswords, rune_mage, high_runes, battle_healer; shieldbearers folded into veteran_techniques, pike_square is a Spearmen doctrine), gear tiers (master_armoury + gear lines), warehouse checklist levels (warehouse_racks = L3, great_storehouse L4, royal_storehouse L5). v2 (26 Sep): Commons & Household rebuilt around a living village (home tiers, War Feast, festivals, Bard's Stage, Rooms to Let, Hall of Heroes, Families, Chapel vs Alehouse); Infirmary moved to Commons; Varied Table merged into Kitchen & Long Table; new Craft node Masters & Apprentices; plain +X% nodes in every branch gained a visible or behavioural hook.
meta.title: Bannerhold tech tree (expanded design)
meta.notes: Design data for the preview page and the later in-game implementation. Layout: screen coordinates with the Banner at (0,0) and y growing DOWN (like DevelopmentScreen): Watch = north (-y), Logistics = east (+x), Commons = south (+y), Craft = west (-x). Tier rings sit at radius ~170-265 (Hamlet), 410-505 (Village), 650-745 (Town) and 890-985 (Castle). The Crown spine spirals clockwise on the ring boundaries (Village NE r330, Town SE r570, Castle SW r810, Kingdom NW r1060). A node with a non-empty 'excludes' list is a pick-one; capstones can be pick-ones too. Goods ids starting with '#' are item tags (any log / any plank / any wool). Coins are always paid first, then goods, all-or-nothing, from the Banner treasury view (buyer inventory, Banner, Warehouse chests). 'time' is study time in in-game days (1 day = 40 real min at x2 day length), which needs a new study timer; tier 1-2 are instant. Building levels and home tiers are recognised from what is built in the room (plaque scan / Requirement checklist, shown as 'next level: add X'); a node unlocks the recognition and perks of a level, and the player or a Builder Upgrade Order meets the checklist. No level depends on a blueprint. 'change' (optional) says what differs from today's code for existing_changed nodes. Ids of existing nodes and upgrades are kept for save compatibility; the Logistics sack/cart/road ids and costs match the logistics build agent's PostRaidUpgrade entries (wire 12-15); warehouse levels use wire 16-18 and the Builder lane 19-20.

type.capstone: big payoff at the end of a branch or a rank seal

status.existing_changed: exists in code but is renamed, moved, re-priced or reworked (see 'change')

size.S: a few hours, reuses an existing hook
size.M: 1-2 days, a new loop or a new item
size.L: a slice of several days, a new system

branches.name: Crown
branches.description: The rank spine: Hamlet, Village, Town, Castle, Kingdom. Each charter opens the next ring of every branch. It spirals outward from the Banner.

branches.name: Watch & Defense
branches.description: Guards, archers, battle roles, Captain's Voice commands, walls, gates, towers and the infirmary: everything that decides a raid.

branches.name: Logistics
branches.description: Couriers, sacks and packs, carts, roads, warehouse capacity and delivery priority. Goods move faster and in bigger loads.

branches.name: Commons & Household
branches.description: Homes and beds, the Tavern and its bard, meals and food variety, morale, festivals and the Blessing shrine.

branches.name: Craft & Production
branches.description: Jobs and workstations, farms and fish, the chains from wood, ore, hide and wool to finished goods, and the tools that make work faster.

tiers.name: Hamlet
tiers.requirement: Raise the Banner. Every Hamlet node is reachable in the first 1-2 hours, before the first raid.

tiers.name: Village
tiers.requirement: Village Charter: stamped automatically when the first raid resolves, win or lose (about 100-120 real min at x2 day length).

tiers.name: Town
tiers.requirement: Town Charter: 15 settlers, 3 raids won, and 2 Village nodes in each of 3 branches.

tiers.name: Castle
tiers.requirement: Castle Charter: 25 settlers, 6 raids won, and stone walls around the Banner.

tiers.name: Kingdom
tiers.requirement: Crown of the Realm: 40 settlers, 12 raids won, one outpost, and an alliance or vassal.

nodes.name: Banner Raised
nodes.offers: Found your hamlet: the Mayor, 4 founder places and ring 1 of every branch.
details: Granted automatically when the Banner is raised (3 logs, 5 cobblestone, 1 campfire)
The Mayor and 3 hireable founders arrive; 4 founder places, and every bed adds one more
Opens every Hamlet node whose own gate is met
The separate 'Banner Raised' seal (id shelter) folds into this one; the id stays, but it is hidden
nodes.flavor: Where the banner stands, the law begins.
nodes.change: Today there are two free auto-granted seals, Settlement Charter and Banner Raised (shelter), and neither does anything. This merges them into one.

nodes.name: Village Charter
nodes.offers: Survive your first raid and the hamlet becomes a Village: ring 2 opens in every branch.
details: Stamps itself when the first raid resolves, win or lose. There is no Learn click
Opens every Village node, including the old post-raid upgrades
Raids from now on: 5-8 raiders every 3-4 in-game days; each victory gives Coins plus a pick of 1 of 3 Blessings
'Village' title on the Banner screen and the map
Gear: opens Gear Tier 1 (Mail: chainmail, shields, turtle shell) for Man-at-Arms-rank guards, Marksmen and level-3 workers
nodes.flavor: They came with torches. We are still here.
nodes.change: Today it is called 'First Raid Aftermath', must be claimed by hand and grants nothing itself. It becomes the auto-stamped Village rank seal, and the id is kept.

nodes.name: Town Charter

cost.other: 15 settlers, 3 raids won, and 2 Village nodes in each of 3 branches

nodes.offers: Become a Town: ring 3 opens, merchants bring fuller purses and raids grow tougher.
details: Opens every Town node
Merchant purse per visit: 12 -> 16 Coins
Town Hall plan: the Mayor's office adds 2 emblem-shop lines and a notice board for quests
Raids grow to 10-15 raiders, and shieldbearers and raider archers join
nodes.flavor: A market cross, a hall, a name on the king's map.

nodes.name: Castle Charter

cost.other: 25 settlers, 6 raids won, stone walls around the Banner

nodes.offers: Become a Castle: ring 4 opens and you raise a Keep, the last stand of your people.
details: Opens every Castle node
Keep building: in raids, civilians shelter inside and take -50% damage; guards within 24 blocks deal +10% damage
Merchant purse 16 -> 20 Coins
Raids grow to 15-25 raiders, with torchbearers and wolves; nemesis captains return holding grudges
Gear: half of Gear Tier 3 (Diamond); the other half is the Master Armoury
nodes.flavor: Stone does not burn.

nodes.name: Crown of the Realm

cost.other: 40 settlers, 12 raids won, 1 outpost, an alliance or a vassal

nodes.offers: Crown yourself: Kingdom rank, two Blessings per victory, and a seat among the rival kingdoms.
details: Kingdom title and a royal banner for every player's Banner
Pick 2 Blessings after each victory (3 with the Cathedral)
Rival kingdoms send envoys: alliances, marriages, spies and declarations of war
Up to 5 outposts
Gear: half of Gear Tier 4 (Netherite, for Captains and level-10 workers); the other half is the Master Armoury
nodes.flavor: Kneel a lord, rise a king.

nodes.name: Barracks & Guard
nodes.offers: Build a Barracks and hire Guards who patrol, answer the alarm and fight beside you.
details: Barracks plan (2 beds) + Guard emblem (3 Coins, 2 iron, 1 leather)
Every guard already uses the full moveset: light, telegraphed heavy, 3-hit combo and shield bash
Well-fed guards regenerate health
nodes.flavor: Every village needs someone awake at night.

nodes.name: Guard Drill
nodes.offers: Guards spar every morning at the Barracks and earn +15% combat XP.
details: Existing: +15% Guard combat XP from real kills (stacks with Shield Wall to +40%)
New: morning drill. After breakfast, off-duty guards pair up and spar in front of the Barracks with the real moveset (no damage) for a few minutes
Guards reach Man-at-Arms rank (leather chest) sooner
nodes.flavor: Sweat in the yard saves blood at the gate.
depends_on: Sparring behaviour (reuses GuardMeleeGoal moves without damage)
nodes.change: It keeps +15% XP and adds a visible morning sparring drill.

nodes.name: Watchtower & Archers

cost.other: 1 Courier-delivered weapon to a Guard (a proof milestone, no Coins)

nodes.offers: Build a Watchtower, hire Archers, and post Guards on the tower.
details: Watchtower plan (banner, 4 ladders) + Archer emblem (3 Coins, 4 arrows, 1 leather)
Tower Post orders for Guards
Couriers keep tower archers stocked with real arrows
nodes.flavor: From the tower you see them before they see you.

nodes.name: Captain's Voice
nodes.offers: Command your soldiers in the fight: one key per role (R knights, G archers, and keys for spearmen, longswords, mages, healers), ordered by what you look at.
details: Tap a role key: the order depends on what you look at
Ground: they form a line there; Enemy: melee charge it, ranged focus it; Wall or tower: archers climb up; your own feet: they follow you
Shift + key: back to posts
Hold the key: dots on the ground show each soldier's place; scroll to widen the line, release to confirm
A short line shows how many heard you, e.g. 'Knights: shield line (4/6)'
nodes.flavor: One shout, and they turn as one.
depends_on: Guard control (per-role keys) - being built now
nodes.change: Replaces the horn + radial idea with the owner's chosen controls (26 Sep).

nodes.name: Raise the Barricades
nodes.offers: When a raid is spotted, sound the order and the whole village turns out to throw up barricades on the spots you marked.
details: Mark barricade spots with the Work Scepter (the Barricade block itself comes with the Builder's Hut)
After a raid warning, 'Raise barricades' on the Banner screen sends idle settlers to place stored barricades (40 HP each), carrying them from the Warehouse (visible)
Raiders already chop through blocking blocks (RaiderBreachGoal); barricades give them a real target
After the raid, settlers pick up any intact barricades
nodes.flavor: Carts on their sides, stakes in the mud: it will do till morning.
nodes.change: v3: the block recipe moved to the Builder's Hut (Builder lane); this node is the village-wide warning-time order.

nodes.name: Defense Plans
nodes.offers: Draw a defense line on the ground and your Builder raises palisade walls, gates and a timber watchtower along it.
details: Defense Plan line tool: mark a wall line; the Builder builds palisade segments along it from your stores
Palisade gates and a timber watchtower blueprint
Each wall block is tagged with its segment kind (palisade, stone, gate) so raids can find weak points
Stone versions need Masonry
nodes.flavor: A line in the dirt today, a wall by the next new moon.
depends_on: Builder lane (being built now: PostRaidUpgrade wire 19)

nodes.name: Shield Wall
nodes.offers: Guards learn the shield wall: the Hold the Line order and +25% combat XP.
details: Existing: +25% Guard combat XP, which stacks with Guard Drill
New: Captain's Voice gains the shield line. Look at the ground and hold the Knights key (R): guards form up shoulder to shoulder on the dots and hold
A holding guard with a shield takes -30% frontal damage and cannot be knocked back
No longer the parent of the Hunters' Lodge, which moves to Craft
nodes.flavor: Lock shields. Nobody steps back.
depends_on: Guard control (per-role keys) - being built now
nodes.change: Renamed from 'Shield Doctrine'. It keeps its XP effect and gains the Hold order. The Hunters' Lodge edge moves to Craft.

nodes.name: Spearmen
nodes.offers: A new battle role: Spearmen fight from the second rank with long reach and brace against charges.
details: Pike Yard plan (checklist: 2 beds, 2 hay bales as drill targets, 1 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 30 floor) + Spearman emblem (4 C, 1 iron, 1 leather)
Spear reach 1.5x normal melee: they strike over the Knights' shield line
Brace: a braced spearman stops and staggers the first enemy that charges him
Own Captain's Voice key (J); spearmen use the guard rank ladder for Gear Tiers
nodes.flavor: Keep them at the end of your spear and they cannot reach you.
depends_on: Battle roles lane (being built now; plan/BATTLE-ROLES.md)
nodes.change: In code today the Spearman and Pike Yard hang off shield_doctrine (no new DevelopmentNode wire id yet); they move here when the tree lands.

nodes.name: Iron Arms Drill
nodes.offers: Veterans wear iron chest and legs, Sergeants full iron: one armour tier earlier.
details: Existing effect: GuardArms dresses Veteran and above in the next rank's kit
Every piece is still taken from the Armoury, a Warehouse or the Banner stores, never conjured
Pairs with the Armoury, which forges the iron
Gear: opens Gear Tier 2 (Plate: iron armour, crossbows) for Veteran guards, Sharpshooters and level-5 workers; any one of Iron Arms Drill, Armoury or Mine, Smelter & Smithy counts
nodes.flavor: Iron on the shoulders of those who earned it.
nodes.change: Today it costs 8 Coins and nothing else. This adds 6 iron so every node costs Coins plus goods.

nodes.name: Longbows
nodes.offers: Archers shoot farther and faster, and loose volleys on your command.
details: Range 18 -> 20 blocks, draw 20 -> 16 ticks (existing ArcherDrill)
New: Volley. Look at an enemy and tap the Archers key (G): every archer in earshot looses at it at once
Pick one: Longbows or Crossbows
Saves that already own the drill keep it, and Crossbows stay locked for them
nodes.flavor: Yew, patience, and forty arrows in the air at once.
depends_on: Guard control (per-role keys) for the Volley
nodes.change: Becomes one side of a pick-one choice against Crossbows, gains the Captain's Voice Volley, and adds string and logs to the Coin-only price.

nodes.name: Crossbows
nodes.offers: Archers switch to crossbows: slower, but every bolt hits hard and punches through shields.
details: Archers wield vanilla crossbows (made by the Smith or bought) and still shoot real arrows
Crossbows are Gear Tier 2 (Plate): an archer needs Sharpshooter rank and the village needs Iron Arms Drill, an Armoury or a Smithy
+40% damage per shot, and it ignores a shieldbearer's frontal block
Reload 30 ticks (a bow draws in 16-20); range 16 blocks
Pierce 1: a bolt can hit a second raider standing in line
nodes.flavor: Any farmhand can learn it in a week. That is the point.

nodes.name: Armoury & Armourer
nodes.offers: An Armourer forges armour and shields for your guards from village iron and leather.
details: Armoury plan + Armourer emblem
Makes leather armour, iron armour and shields from stored goods (these Production recipes already exist)
Guards dress from the Armoury first, then the Warehouse
Gear can still be crafted by players or bought
Gear: opens Gear Tier 2 (Plate: iron armour, crossbows) for Veteran guards, Sharpshooters and level-5 workers; any one of Iron Arms Drill, Armoury or Mine, Smelter & Smithy counts
nodes.flavor: A guard is only as good as the steel the village gives him.
nodes.change: Today a FUTURE placeholder that cannot be bought (4 iron blocks). The building, the profession and its recipes already exist. The price drops to 12 iron.

nodes.name: Watchfires & Great Bell
nodes.offers: Earlier raid warnings, and an alarm bell heard across the whole village.
details: Raid warning comes 30 in-game minutes earlier for each staffed Watchtower (max +1 h, so up to 2 h of warning)
The warning shows the raid's direction on the Banner screen and the map
Alarm bell radius 16 -> 32 blocks, and civilians run to shelter 25% faster
Off-duty guards within 48 blocks answer the bell
nodes.flavor: Smoke on the ridge - ring it, ring it now!
depends_on: Scout-warning timer (owner decision: ~1 in-game hour, earlier with a better watch)

nodes.name: Manned Palisade
nodes.offers: Your palisade becomes a fighting wall: guards shut the gates on the alarm, archers walk the wall, and the timber holds twice as long.
details: Palisade segments built from Defense Plans get double HP (80); gates are shut by guards on the alarm and opened for settlers
Archers can be sent up onto the palisade walkway (Captain's Voice: look at the wall, tap G)
Raiders head for the gate or the weakest gap and must breach it
Settlers repair damaged palisade after raids with the existing nail and chisel repair loop
Pick one: Palisade or Ditch & Stakes. Either one upgrades to Stone Walls at Town rank
nodes.flavor: Sharpened oak, shoulder to shoulder, all the way round.

nodes.name: Ditch & Stakes
nodes.offers: Settlers dig a staked ditch. Raiders crossing it slow to a crawl, and there is no gate to lose.
details: Draw a ditch line with the Defense Plan tool; the Builder and idle settlers dig it 2 blocks deep and set stakes
Raiders in the ditch move 40% slower and take 1 damage per second
It cannot be breached, only crossed; your own people use the bridges you place
Pick one: Palisade or Ditch & Stakes. Either one upgrades to Stone Walls at Town rank
nodes.flavor: Let them come. Let them come slowly.

nodes.name: Stone Walls & Arrow Slits

cost.other: Own Manned Palisade or Ditch & Stakes

nodes.offers: Stone walls three times as strong, and arrow slits that make your towers deadly.
details: Stone segments built with Masonry get 240 HP (palisade 40, Manned Palisade 80); the Builder converts palisade in place
Arrow slit block: an archer behind it takes -60% ranged damage and gets +2 range
Stone gate with 3x the HP of a palisade gate; it closes instantly on the alarm
Required for the Castle Charter
nodes.flavor: What the axe cannot cut, the fire cannot eat.

nodes.name: Veteran Techniques
nodes.offers: Guards master their moveset: harder bashes, a four-strike combo and shield-breaking heavies.
details: Every guard today knows the light attack, the heavy, the 3-hit combo and the bash; this node upgrades them and takes nothing away
Shield Bash: -30% cooldown, +0.5 s stagger, and it opens a shieldbearer's guard for 2 s
Combo: a 4th finisher strike (+30% damage) and a combo window 4 ticks longer
Heavy: breaks a raised shield and knocks brutes back 1 block
The upgraded moves are for Man-at-Arms rank and up; Recruits keep the basics

Tower shields: Veteran-rank Knights can carry a tower shield that blocks 80% of frontal arrows and anchors the shield line (replaces the separate Shieldbearer role idea; the owner's roles are Knights, Archers, Spearmen, Longswordsmen, Mages and Healers)
nodes.flavor: Watch the shoulder, not the blade.
nodes.change: Builds on the existing GuardMove / GuardMeleeGoal moveset. The values in GuardMove get upgraded versions, read through Development.

nodes.name: Longswordsmen
nodes.offers: A new battle role: two-handed longswordsmen who break shields and cut through crowds.
details: Sword Hall plan (checklist: 2 beds, 1 anvil, 1 grindstone, 1 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 30 floor) + Longswordsman emblem (5 C, 3 iron, 2 leather)
Two-handed sweeps hit several raiders at once; heavy strikes break a raised shield
No shield of their own: keep them behind the Knights until the line breaks
Own Captain's Voice key (K); longswordsmen use the guard rank ladder for Gear Tiers
nodes.flavor: Two hands, one blade, and plenty of room around him.
depends_on: Battle roles lane (being built now; plan/BATTLE-ROLES.md)
nodes.change: The roles lane lists 'spearmen or shieldbearers' as the requirement; Shieldbearers is not a role, so it is spearmen. In code today it hangs off shield_doctrine.

nodes.name: Rune Mage
nodes.offers: A new battle role: a Rune Mage who spends rune charges on spells that turn a fight.
details: Rune Hall plan (checklist: 1 enchanting table, 4 amethyst blocks, 4 bookshelves, 1 door, 3 lights, 25 floor) + Rune Mage emblem (6 C, 8 lapis, 4 amethyst shards, 1 book)
Spells cost rune charges: 3 max, +1 every 60 s; a Ward spell lasts 5 s
Rune Stones (1 amethyst shard + 2 lapis + 1 smooth stone -> 2) are stocked to the Rune Hall by Couriers; each stone gives +1 charge
Mage cap: 1 (2 with High Runes); own Captain's Voice key (N)
nodes.flavor: Old words, cut into stone, and the stone remembers them.
depends_on: Battle roles lane (being built now; plan/BATTLE-ROLES.md)
nodes.change: In code today the Rune Mage hangs off hearth_doctrine plus a built Rune Hall; mage cap 2 at 20+ settlers until high_runes exists.

nodes.name: Master Armoury
nodes.offers: Your Armourer and Smith learn to work diamond and netherite: Gear Tier 3 for Sergeants, Master Archers and level-8 workers, and with the Crown, Tier 4 for Captains.
details: Gear Tier 3 (Diamond: all diamond gear, trident, mace) with the Castle Charter
Gear Tier 4 (Netherite) with the Crown of the Realm
The Armoury can issue the new tiers to guards of the right rank (GearGate: rank AND village knowledge)
The settler sheet shows 'next gear tier: <rank> + <knowledge>' for every soldier
nodes.flavor: Diamond is only a stone until a master knows where to strike it.
depends_on: Gear tiers (GearTier/GearGate built by the gear agent; resolves node:master_armoury)

nodes.name: High Runes
nodes.offers: Your mages master the high runes: a second Rune Mage, more stones from every carving, and longer wards.
details: Mage cap 1 -> 2
Rune Stone carving makes 3 instead of 2
Ward lasts 6 s instead of 5 s
nodes.flavor: The high runes are not spoken. They are sung.
depends_on: Battle roles lane (being built now; plan/BATTLE-ROLES.md)

nodes.name: Order of Knights
nodes.offers: Mounted knights: your best guards (the R-key Knights) take to horseback, charge through raider lines and run down archers.
details: Up to 4 Sergeant or Captain Knights ride horses from your Stable (Knights = the guard group, Captain's Voice key R)
The Charge order sends knights trampling through a line: 8 damage plus knockback
Knights catch fleeing raiders and wolves
Pick one: Knights or Pike Square
nodes.flavor: Hooves on the frost, lances down.

nodes.name: Pike Square
nodes.offers: Spearmen doctrine: your Spearmen form a braced square, and nothing gets through, not brutes, not wolves.
details: Square formation: all-round brace, with no flank penalty while in the square
Brace strike +50%
Chargers (brutes, wolves) are stopped dead against a braced square
Pick one: Order of Knights or Pike Square
nodes.flavor: Ash shafts, iron heads, and not one step back.
depends_on: Battle roles lane (being built now; plan/BATTLE-ROLES.md)

nodes.name: Warehouse & Courier
nodes.offers: Build a Warehouse and hire Couriers who carry goods to one shared store.
details: Warehouse plan + Courier emblem (2 Coins, 1 chest, 2 leather)

Warehouse levels come from the plaque checklist, never a blueprint. L1 Storeroom manages 16 containers (4 storage, 1 door, 2 lights, 25 floor); L2 Stockroom manages 32 (16 storage, a ledger desk, 4 lights, solid floor). Higher levels need Storehouse, Great Storehouse and Royal Storehouse
Containers beyond the cap show as 'not managed (warehouse full)'; nothing breaks
Base Courier load: 8 items per trip
nodes.flavor: A place for everything, and a boy to carry it there.
nodes.change: Renamed only, from 'Stores & Roads'; the roads now live in Paved Roads.

nodes.name: Stout Straps
nodes.offers: Couriers carry 2 more items and pick up two different jobs on one trip.
details: Existing: a flat +2 carry that stacks with every sack and cart tier
New: pickup batching. A Courier with room left takes a second request on the way (e.g. logs to the Warehouse, then bread to the Tavern) instead of walking back empty
nodes.flavor: Double-stitched, and it will outlive the courier.
depends_on: Pickup batching (listed as a later idea by the logistics agent)
nodes.change: It keeps +2 carry and gains two-job trips.

nodes.name: Paved Roads
nodes.offers: Every settler walks 15% faster on roads: dirt path, gravel, cobble, stone and bricks.
details: +15% walking speed (server config logistics.pavedRoadsPercent) on blocks in the hearthstead:roads tag (dirt path, gravel, cobble, stone bricks, bricks)
Hand carts roll 10% faster on roads
Raiders get no bonus
nodes.flavor: Lay a road and the village grows along it.
depends_on: Built by the logistics agent now (PostRaidUpgrade wire 14)

nodes.name: Courier Satchel
nodes.offers: Sack tier 1: Couriers carry 50% more (8 -> 12 per trip), and you can see the satchel on their hip.
details: Carry = 8 x (100 + sack% + cart%) / 100, + 2 Stout Straps, + Trade skill (0-3)
The weight budget scales with capacity (16 x capacity / 8), so bigger sacks and carts move stone and logs too
Visible: each sack tier draws on the Courier model (satchel, then leather pack, then frame pack)
Price unchanged (4 Coins); the logistics agent keeps it as is
nodes.flavor: Oiled canvas and a good buckle.
depends_on: Sack model layer on the Courier (not in the logistics agent's current scope)
nodes.change: The carry effect is unchanged; the satchel becomes visible on the Courier.

nodes.name: Leather Pack
nodes.offers: Sack tier 2: Couriers carry double (8 -> 16 per trip).
details: Sack +100% (replaces the Satchel's +50%)
Worker Packs follow the sack tier, so Lumberers and Farmers carry more too
nodes.flavor: Cow-hide on the back, wool on the shoulders.
depends_on: Built by the logistics agent now (PostRaidUpgrade wire 12)

nodes.name: Frame Pack
nodes.offers: Sack tier 3: Couriers carry 2.5x (8 -> 20 per trip).
details: Sack +150%
With a Hand Cart: 8 x (100 + 150 + 200) / 100 = 36 items per trip (38 with Straps)
Lumberers and Farmers carry at the same tier (Worker Packs)
nodes.flavor: A frame of ash, and a man can carry a calf.
depends_on: Built by the logistics agent now (PostRaidUpgrade wire 13)

nodes.name: Hand Cart
nodes.offers: Couriers push a real, visible hand cart: +200% carry.
details: Cart +200% of base: with the Satchel, 8 x 3.5 = 28 items per trip
+10% speed on roads, -15% off-road (server config: logistics.handCartPercent / handCartRoughPercent)
A visible cart model rolls behind the Courier
nodes.flavor: Two wheels, two handles, and no more sore backs.
depends_on: Built by the logistics agent now (visible cart)
nodes.change: Today it is an invisible flat +8. It becomes a visible cart with a percentage bonus and road/off-road speed, and 12 planks, 4 logs and 2 iron join the 8 Coins.

nodes.name: Worker Packs
nodes.offers: Lumberers and Farmers carry at the settlement's sack tier (at least +50%).
details: Minimum tier 1 = the old 3/2 behaviour (8 -> 12)
Leather Pack -> 16, Frame Pack -> 20 per trip
Visible: Lumberers and Farmers wear the same sack model as the Couriers
nodes.flavor: Fewer walks to the store, more trees down.
nodes.change: Today a fixed x1.5. It now follows the sack tier (logistics agent).

nodes.name: Swift Couriers
nodes.offers: Couriers walk 10% faster everywhere and jog when a delivery is urgent.
details: +10% Courier walking speed; stacks with Paved Roads
Visible: Couriers jog (run animation) on Urgent requests and when restocking arrows during a raid
nodes.flavor: Light boots, and no dawdling at the well.
depends_on: Built by the logistics agent now (PostRaidUpgrade wire 15)

nodes.name: Storehouse (Warehouse L3)
nodes.offers: The plaque now recognises Warehouse level 3, the Storehouse: 64 managed containers, with labelled shelves your Couriers can read.
details: L3 Storehouse checklist (plaque scan): 32 storage, a ledger desk (lectern or cartography table), 4 labels (signs or item frames), 6 lights, 100 floor, solid floor
Managed containers 32 -> 64 once the room meets the checklist; the plaque shows 'next level: add X' until then
You or a Builder Upgrade Order add the missing pieces
A level built above what you have unlocked counts as your highest unlocked level, and the UI names the missing node
Old saves keep at least the level that covers their containers (up to L3)
nodes.flavor: Shelves to the rafters, and a label on every one.
depends_on: Warehouse checklist levels (being built now: PostRaidUpgrade wire 16, WarehouseLevels)
nodes.change: v3: this is now the warehouse agent's L3 recognition gate. The earlier 64 -> 96 cap idea is dropped; the Storage Rack display block and sort-by-kind filing stay as a future idea.

nodes.name: Courier's Ledger
nodes.offers: Set each building's delivery priority and minimum stock; urgent needs are served first.
details: Per-building priority: Low / Normal / Urgent (roadmap M5)
Minimum stock rules, e.g. keep 32 arrows at the Watchtower and 16 bread at the Tavern (roadmap M3)
Couriers take Urgent jobs first, then the oldest request
Set from the Warehouse screen
nodes.flavor: Arrows first. The baker can wait.

nodes.name: Coster's Cart
nodes.offers: Two-wheeled cart, cart tier 2: +300% carry.
details: Cart +300% (replaces the Hand Cart's +200%): with a Frame Pack, 8 x 5.5 = 44 items per trip
Needs roads: off-road it is as slow as a hand cart
Timber Beams come from the Sawmill
nodes.flavor: Iron-shod wheels, and a coster who knows every rut.
depends_on: Cart entity (shared with the Hand Cart)

nodes.name: Porters' Guild
nodes.offers: Heavy loads: +50 points in the carry formula, but Couriers walk 10% slower.
details: Frame Pack + Hand Cart 36 -> 40 per trip; Coster's Cart 44 -> 48
Courier walking speed -10%
Visible: Porters carry towering, strapped-up loads, and two Porters can shoulder a whole chest between them to move a store
Pick one: Porters or Runners
nodes.flavor: Bent backs, full stores.

nodes.name: Runners' Guild
nodes.offers: Swift feet: Couriers walk 15% faster and take their next job the instant one is free.
details: +15% Courier speed (stacks with Swift Couriers and Paved Roads)
No idle pause between deliveries
Runners' relay: on a raid warning, a Runner sprints the news to every outlying worker, who heads home at once instead of waiting for the bell
Pick one: Porters or Runners
nodes.flavor: There and back before the bread cools.

nodes.name: Great Storehouse (Warehouse L4)
nodes.offers: The plaque now recognises the Great Storehouse: 128 managed containers for a town's worth of goods.
details: L4 checklist (plaque scan): 64 storage, a ledger desk, 8 labels, 10 lights, 2 doors, 200 floor, solid floor
Managed containers 64 -> 128
You or a Builder Upgrade Order add the missing pieces
nodes.flavor: Two doors: one for what comes in, one for what goes out.
depends_on: Warehouse checklist levels (being built now: PostRaidUpgrade wire 17; in code it hangs off the Village Charter until town_charter exists)

nodes.name: Mule Carts
nodes.offers: Mule-drawn carts, cart tier 3: +400% carry, and 20% faster on roads.
details: Stable building; each mule pulls one cart for a Courier or a Carter
Mules eat hay from the Warehouse
On the alarm, spooked mules shelter in the Stable
nodes.flavor: Stubborn, hungry, and worth ten men.

nodes.name: Royal Storehouse (Warehouse L5)
nodes.offers: The plaque now recognises the Royal Storehouse: 256 managed containers, the granary of a castle.
details: L5 checklist (plaque scan): 128 storage, 2 ledger desks, 16 labels, 16 lights, 2 doors, 320 floor, solid floor
Managed containers 128 -> 256
You or a Builder Upgrade Order add the missing pieces
nodes.flavor: The king's tithe-barn has nothing on ours.
depends_on: Warehouse checklist levels (being built now: PostRaidUpgrade wire 18)

nodes.name: Outposts & Caravans
nodes.offers: Found mine, farm and watch outposts, linked to home by scheduled caravans on the King's Road.
details: Outpost Banner: a small claim with 2-4 workers and one building, up to 256 blocks away (1 outpost at Castle, 5 at Kingdom)
A Carter runs a timetable between outpost and Warehouse; cargo moves as data while chunks are unloaded
King's Road: +30% speed on stone-brick roads, and a rich merchant (32-Coin purse, rare goods) every 3 days
Outposts and caravans can be raided or ambushed (smaller events)
nodes.flavor: The realm is only as wide as its roads.

nodes.name: Lumber Camp
nodes.offers: Build a Lumber Camp, hire a Lumberer, and get the Work Scepter.
details: Lumber Camp plan + Lumberer emblem (1 Coin, 2 flint)
Work Scepter recipe for marking work areas
nodes.flavor: First the axe, then everything else.

nodes.name: Builder's Hut
nodes.offers: Hire a Builder: they fill the gaps on any building's checklist for you, build starter blueprints, and make barricades.
details: Builder's Hut plan + Builder emblem
Upgrade Orders: on any plaque that says 'next level: add X', order the Builder to add the missing pieces from your stores (beds, lights, labels, a planked floor...)
Starter blueprints (optional): Cottage, Warehouse, Tavern, Barracks, Builder's Hut. Building levels and home tiers never depend on blueprints; they come only from the plaque checklist
Barricade block recipe: a first-raid village can rush barricades without Defense Plans
Stone floors in Upgrade Orders need Masonry
nodes.flavor: Tell me what the room is missing, and I will fetch my hammer.
depends_on: Builder lane (being built now: BUILDERS_HUT + BUILDER, shared BuildingLevelChecklist)
nodes.change: For now the Builder's Hut and Builder emblem ride on timber_rights in code; they move to this node when the tree implementation lands.

nodes.name: Sharpened Axes
nodes.offers: Lumberers whet their axes on a grindstone and fell each tree 10% faster, and they replant as they go.
details: Existing: felling time -10%
New: every 8 trees, the Lumberer whets his axe at the Lumber Camp grindstone (sparks and sound)
New: the Lumberer plants a sapling in every stump he leaves, so the forest grows back
nodes.flavor: A keen edge is half the day's work.
depends_on: Grindstone visit + replant step in LumbererWorkGoal
nodes.change: It keeps -10% felling and gains the grindstone visit and replanting.

nodes.name: Fields & Farmer
nodes.offers: Build a Farmhouse and hire a Farmer who sows, reaps and stores wheat.
details: Farmhouse plan + Farmer emblem (2 Coins, 8 seeds, 1 leather)
Crop Rotation research: +15% crop growth
nodes.flavor: Bread starts in the mud.
nodes.change: Renamed only, from 'Cultivated Ground'.

nodes.name: Fishery
nodes.offers: Build a Fishery; a Fisher lands food and rare catches for trade.
details: Fishery plan + Fisher emblem (2 Coins, 2 string, 1 leather)
Rare fish (perch, trout, pike, golden char) sell to merchants
nodes.flavor: The river pays in silver scales.
nodes.change: Renamed only, from 'Shore Provisions'.

nodes.name: Fisher's Nets
nodes.offers: Casts finish 10% sooner, and the Fisher sets a net with a floating buoy that fills while he rests.
details: Existing: cast cycle -10%
New: the Fisher sets a net in the water (a visible buoy); it holds 1 fish per in-game hour, up to 4, which he hauls in at the start of work
nodes.flavor: Mend the net, and the net feeds you while you sleep.
depends_on: Net buoy block + haul step in FisherWorkGoal
nodes.change: It keeps -10% cast time and gains a passive net.

nodes.name: Sawmill & Sawyer
nodes.offers: A Sawyer turns logs into planks and Timber Beams.
details: Sawmill plan + Sawyer emblem
Seasoned Timber research: sawing -15% time
Timber Beams feed the Coster's Cart, Deep Mine and Guild Halls
nodes.flavor: The saw sings; the village grows.
nodes.change: Renamed from 'Guild Doctrine'. The ACTIVE/DORMANT 'primary tradition' badge is dropped because nothing reads it.

nodes.name: Mill, Bakery & Pasture
nodes.offers: Millers, Bakers, Herders and Butchers: bread in bulk, wool, leather and meat.
details: Mill, Bakery, Pasture and Butcher plans + Miller, Baker, Herder and Butcher emblems (2 Coins + goods each)
Flour -> bread in bulk frees the Innkeeper and fills the meal reserve
Wool feeds beds and Wool Bolts; hides feed the Tannery
Better Yeast research: baking -15%
nodes.flavor: Grind, knead, shear: the steady heartbeat of a village.
depends_on: Emblem entries + release GameTests for 4 trades
nodes.change: Today a FUTURE placeholder. The buildings, professions, HerderWorkGoal and the Production recipes all exist.

nodes.name: Hunters' Lodge
nodes.offers: A Hunter ranges beyond the walls and brings back meat, feathers and hides.
details: Hunters' Lodge plan + Hunter emblem (4 Coins, 12 arrows, 2 leather)
Carcasses are butchered at the lodge table into meat, feathers and hides
nodes.flavor: The forest gives, if you know where to look.
nodes.change: Moved from Watch (under Shield Doctrine) to Craft. Cost unchanged; it now needs only the Village Charter.

nodes.name: Tannery & Tanner

cost.other: Own the Hunters' Lodge or Mill, Bakery & Pasture (a hide source)

nodes.offers: A Tanner cures hides into leather and Cured Hide, and you can sew yourself a Pedlar's Sack.
details: Tannery plan + Tanner emblem (the building and its recipes exist)
Cured Hide feeds the Porters' Guild and Armoury gear: the tanner -> leather -> packs chain
Player item: Pedlar's Sack recipe (leather + cured hide), a bundle-style bag with 9 extra slots
Tanning Acid research (-15% time) can now be started
nodes.flavor: It stinks. It pays.
nodes.change: Split out of the Craft and Industry placeholder.

nodes.name: Mine, Smelter & Smithy
nodes.offers: Mine ore, smelt iron and forge tools, and workers holding iron tools work faster.
details: Mine, Smelter and Smithy plans + Miner, Smelter and Smith emblems (MinerWorkGoal and the recipes exist)
Smith makes iron tools and swords for equipment requests
Tool tiers: a worker holding an iron tool works 10% faster (diamond 20%)
Blast Bellows research (smelting -15%) can now be started
Gear: opens Gear Tier 2 (Plate: iron armour, crossbows) for Veteran guards, Sharpshooters and level-5 workers; any one of Iron Arms Drill, Armoury or Mine, Smelter & Smithy counts
nodes.flavor: Stone to ore, ore to bloom, bloom to blade.
depends_on: Tool-tier speed hook in the work goals
nodes.change: Reuses the Craft and Industry placeholder id for mining and metal. Tannery, Carpenter, Mason and Weaver split off.

nodes.name: Masonry
nodes.offers: Your Builder learns stone: stone wall segments, a stone gatehouse, a stone watchtower, and stone floors in Upgrade Orders.
details: Builder can lay stone wall segments and a stone gatehouse along Defense Plan lines
Stone watchtower blueprint and stone variants of the starter blueprints
Upgrade Orders can lay stone or cobble floors (e.g. a Warehouse's 'solid floor'); plank floors work without Masonry
Unlocks no building level: levels stay checklist-only
nodes.flavor: Timber rots. Stone remembers.
depends_on: Builder lane (being built now: PostRaidUpgrade wire 20)

nodes.name: Carpenter, Mason & Weaver
nodes.offers: Workshops for furniture, stone bricks and Wool Bolts, the stuff towns are built from.
details: Carpenter, Mason and Weaver plans + emblems (the recipes exist)
Masons cut stone bricks for walls, houses and charters
Weavers turn wool into Wool Bolts for beds, banners and the Crown
With a Mason, settlers repair and upgrade buildings 20% faster
nodes.flavor: Measure twice, cut once, and the town stands a hundred years.
nodes.change: Split out of the Craft and Industry placeholder.

nodes.name: Charcoal Kilns
nodes.offers: The Smelter burns its own charcoal from logs: smelting 25% faster, with no coal needed.
details: Smelter converts logs -> charcoal as fuel automatically
Smelting -25% time
Pick one: Kilns or Deep Mine
nodes.flavor: Smoke all night, iron all day.

nodes.name: Deep Mine
nodes.offers: The Miner digs two levels deeper: +1 ore on 15% of ore blocks, and a chance of gold.
details: Mine shaft depth +2 levels
15% of ore blocks yield +1 ore
Gold ore can appear in the Miner's haul
Pick one: Kilns or Deep Mine
nodes.flavor: Deeper, lads. The good stuff is always deeper.

nodes.name: Masters & Apprentices
nodes.offers: Skilled workers become Masters and take an Apprentice who follows them and learns twice as fast.
details: A settler at trade level 5+ can be named Master; their plaque title reads 'Master Smith <name>'
Assign any settler as their Apprentice: the Apprentice works beside the Master, copying their animations, and earns double trade XP
Wits matters: the Apprentice earns +1% more XP per Wits point above 15
When a Master dies, their Apprentice inherits the workshop at the Master's level minus 2
nodes.flavor: Watch my hands, not my face.

nodes.name: Guild Halls
nodes.offers: Each trade raises its own guild hall with a banner: more hands in every workshop, Fine goods, and a forge that mends the guard's gear.
details: +1 worker slot in every production building; each guild hangs its banner over its workshops
Crafters at trade level 5+ sometimes make Fine goods that sell for +50% (GoodsQuality exists for fish)
After each raid the Smithy repairs damaged guard gear for free (materials only)
Guild feast day: once per week, each guild's workers take the afternoon off at the Tavern (+10 morale)
nodes.flavor: Every master has a hall; every hall has a feast day.

nodes.name: Houses & Lodging
nodes.offers: Build Houses and a Lodging; every bed beyond the 4 founders lets one more settler live here.
details: House (up to 4 beds) and Lodging (up to 8 beds) plans
Population = beds (minimum 4 founders)

New: every house plaque shows its home tier and a 'next level: add X' checklist (Hut, then Cottage, Townhouse, Manor as those nodes are learned). Tiers come from what is built in the room, never from a blueprint
nodes.flavor: Four walls, a door and a fire: now it is home.
nodes.change: Renamed from 'Home'. The plaque also shows the home tier (label only).

nodes.name: Hearth Fires
nodes.offers: At dusk the village gathers round the fire to eat and talk, and warm homes keep hunger down at night.
details: Existing: night-time hunger drain -10%
New: evening gathering. At dusk, free settlers sit in a ring round the Banner fire (or a house hearth) for a while, eating and chatting with speech bubbles; each gets +3 'good company' morale
New: a house with a campfire, furnace or fireplace sends up chimney smoke, so you can see which homes are warm
nodes.flavor: A banked fire, a full belly and someone to talk to.
nodes.change: Renamed from 'Warm Homes'. It keeps -10% night hunger and gains the dusk gathering and chimney smoke.

nodes.name: Tavern & Trade
nodes.offers: Build a Tavern and a Trading Post; hire an Innkeeper and a Trader.
details: Tavern plan (a bell, which can be copper) + Innkeeper emblem: meals, ale, recruitment and the evening bard
Trading Post plan + Trader emblem: sell surplus for Coins
Recruits cost 25% less with an Innkeeper
First step of the Tavern ladder: Bard's Stage, then Rooms to Let, then Hall of Revels
nodes.flavor: Every road ends at a tavern door.

nodes.name: Cottages
nodes.offers: Home tier 1: the plaque now recognises Cottages. Give a House a bed for everyone, a chest and a flower pot or carpet, and its family makes it theirs.
details: Cottage checklist (plaque scan): a bed per resident + 1 chest + 1 flower pot or carpet. Met: the plaque reads 'Cottage of <family>'; not met: it shows 'next level: add 1 flower pot'. You or a Builder Upgrade Order add the pieces
Existing effect: residents with a claimed bed get +2 morale
Morning routine: residents sweep the doorstep or water the flowers before work (a short idle animation)
Travellers who pass 3 or more Cottages are keener to stay, adding +1 candidate to the recruit pool at the Tavern
Home ladder: Cottage, then Townhouse, then Manor
nodes.flavor: Straw is for horses. Flowers are for the sill.
depends_on: Home-tier checklist on HOUSE (Requirement tiers + plaque 'next level' line)
nodes.change: Renamed from 'Sturdy Beds' and turned into home tier 1. It keeps the +2 bed morale, and the Cottage check, the family sign and the morning routine are added.

nodes.name: Feather Quilts
nodes.offers: Settlers who sleep a full night under quilts wake up Well Rested and work faster all morning.
details: Existing: sleep energy regain +20%
New: Well Rested. A settler who slept the whole night in a quilted bed wakes with a 'Well Rested' bubble and works 10% faster until noon
Settlers who were woken by the alarm do not get it, so a night raid costs you the morning
nodes.flavor: Goose down: a lord's luxury, now a peasant's right.
nodes.change: It keeps +20% sleep energy and gains the visible Well Rested morning buff.

nodes.name: Scholar's Study & Library

cost.other: Everyone housed for 1 day + 5 equipment requests served (existing gate)

nodes.offers: A Scholar researches upgrades you choose, and a Library makes every project cheaper.
details: Architect's Study plan + Scholar emblem; the project scroll on the lectern fills as research progresses
Research projects: Seasoned Timber, Crop Rotation and Guard Drill now; Better Yeast, Blast Bellows and Tanning Acid open with their trades
Library plan (moved here from the Hall and Learning placeholder): research goods -25% (the Costs discount exists)
The Scholar shortens Town and Castle study timers by 25%
nodes.flavor: Ink is cheaper than blood.
nodes.change: Renamed from 'Commons Doctrine'. It also grants the Library plan (the building and discount exist) and speeds the new study timers.

nodes.name: Bard's Stage
nodes.offers: Raise a stage in the Tavern: the bard plays to a crowd, settlers dance, and travellers throw Coins.
details: New block: Bard's Stage. At dusk the bard performs from it and free settlers gather, clap and dance (visible dance loop)
Evening morale lift 5 -> 8 (TavernBard.EVENING_LIFT), with two sets per evening
Travellers (never your own settlers) tip 1 Coin each, max 3 per evening; the Coins land on the stage
Settlers who danced wake Well Rested
nodes.flavor: A song for the living, a song for the dead, and one more for the road.

nodes.name: Kitchen & Long Table
nodes.offers: A Cook feeds the village at one long table, and settlers start to crave favourite foods.
details: Kitchen and Dining Hall plans + Cook emblem (the buildings, profession, recipes and the Dining Hall recruit discount exist)
Noon meal: settlers walk to the long table and eat together (visible); stews and pies count as 2 meals
Cravings: a settler shows a craved food in a thought bubble; serving it gives +5 morale
Variety: 3 or more different foods in the last 5 meals gives -10% hunger drain
Dining Hall: recruit price -25% (with the Innkeeper, the cap is -50%)
nodes.flavor: Everyone eats at the long table, and everyone has an opinion about the stew.
nodes.change: Split out of the Hall and Learning placeholder. It absorbs the old 'Varied Table' stat node as cravings you can see.

nodes.name: War Feast
nodes.offers: When a raid is spotted, call a feast at the Banner: the village eats together and faces the night unafraid.
details: After a raid warning, 'Call the War Feast' on the Banner screen sets out long tables at the Banner (uses 12 meals + 4 ale from the stores)
Settlers and guards gather, eat and toast (visible event, cheering and a war-horn sound)
Guards who ate: +10% damage, +20 morale, and courage for the whole raid (they never flee or break formation)
Civilians who ate walk calmly to shelter instead of panicking, and nobody freezes in the open
Once per raid; it needs at least 5 real minutes of warning
nodes.flavor: Eat, drink, and let them hear us singing from the treeline.
depends_on: Feast gathering event at the Banner
Courage flag for guards and civilians

nodes.name: Townhouses
nodes.offers: Home tier 2: the plaque now recognises Townhouses. Build a second floor and furnish it: 6 beds, couples move in together, and skilled travellers take notice.
details: Townhouse checklist (plaque scan): 2 floors, a table, a bookshelf and 2 lights. Met: the plaque and a door banner show 'Townhouse'; the plaque lists what is missing. You or a Builder Upgrade Order add the pieces
House bed cap 4 -> 6 (Lodging 8 -> 10): room for more settlers
Couples can share a Townhouse (they marry with Families & School)
With 2 or more Townhouses, travellers of trade level 2-3 start to appear at the Tavern
nodes.flavor: Build up, not out, and put a window box on every sill.
depends_on: Traveller skill roll by home tier

nodes.name: Wayside Chapel
nodes.offers: A small chapel: 4 Blessing cards after every victory, a reroll, and a candle for every soul lost.
details: Blessing offer 3 -> 4 cards, plus one free reroll of the whole offer per victory
After each victory the village gathers at the chapel for a short service (+5 morale)
A candle is lit on the altar for every settler who has died; they stay lit
Pick one: Chapel or Alehouse. The Chapel path leads to the Cathedral
nodes.flavor: Leave a coin, say a name, and the road is kinder.
depends_on: Roguelike Blessings expansion (today 3 blessings: Warden's Oath, Hearthward, Thorned Roads)

nodes.name: Alehouse
nodes.offers: A proper alehouse: settlers stop for a pint after work, and feasts and festivals come round far more often.
details: After work, settlers stop at the Tavern for an ale (visible mugs and laughter bubbles): +3 morale
War Feast and Festivals cost half the food, and Festivals can be held every 2 days instead of every 3
Every ale sold to a traveller: +1 Coin
Pick one: Chapel or Alehouse. The Alehouse path leads to the Hall of Revels
nodes.flavor: Brewed on Tuesday, gone by Thursday.

nodes.name: Infirmary
nodes.offers: Downed settlers are carried to the Infirmary instead of dying, and rest there until they are whole.
details: Infirmary plan (the building exists; in code it now opens with the Village Charter); Healers are hired here with Battle Healers
A settler at 0 HP goes down for 60 s, and a guard or the Healer carries them in on their back (visible)
Patients rest in Infirmary beds and heal 1 HP every 2 s; wounded guards return to duty 50% sooner
Without an Infirmary, death is permanent (owner decision)
Cross-link to Watch: the raid report lists who the Infirmary saved
nodes.flavor: Boil the water, and fetch the priest only if I say so.
nodes.change: Moved from Watch to Commons, where it sits with the other life-and-care nodes; Watch cross-links to it. Today the building is listed under the Hall and Learning placeholder and does nothing.

nodes.name: Manors
nodes.offers: Home tier 3: the plaque now recognises Manors. Furnish a grand house and it draws master newcomers, raises bigger families, and gives the village an Elder.
details: Manor checklist (plaque scan): 8+ beds, a bookshelf, a carpet, glass windows and 2 lights per room. Met: the plaque and a gold door banner show 'Manor'; otherwise 'next level: add X'. You or a Builder Upgrade Order add the pieces
Master travellers (trade level 4-5) only visit a village that has a Manor
Family size: up to 1 child in a Cottage, 2 in a Townhouse and 3 in a Manor
The Manor's eldest resident becomes the Village Elder: neighbours within 16 blocks get +2 morale, and the Elder gives the Mayor's speech at festivals
nodes.flavor: The oak panelling came from the lord's own forest.
depends_on: Traveller skill roll by home tier

nodes.name: Rooms to Let
nodes.offers: Guest rooms turn the Tavern into a famous inn: travellers stay, pay, and bring stories and surprises.
details: The plaque now recognises Tavern level 2, the Inn (checklist: 3 guest beds, a second storage, 2 more lights; 'next level: add X'). You or a Builder Upgrade Order add the pieces; no blueprint needed
Guest rooms: up to 3 travellers stay for 2 nights and pay 1 Coin per night plus 1 per meal (TavernGuestPayment)
Fame: the Tavern sign earns stars as guests leave happy; each star makes a weekly visitor event more likely
Visitor events: a wandering knight who spars with your guards (guard XP), a rich trader with a 32-Coin purse, or a storyteller (+10 morale)
Recruiting a guest who stayed costs 25% less
nodes.flavor: The best beds between here and the capital, and the loudest common room.

nodes.name: Harvest & Midsummer Festivals
nodes.offers: Hold village festivals: bunting and lanterns go up, the bard plays, crowds come to spend, and the whole village works faster the next day.
details: The Mayor calls a Harvest Festival or Midsummer at the Banner (every 3 in-game days; every 2 with the Alehouse)
Decorations appear: bunting between houses, lanterns and a maypole at Midsummer; the bard plays and settlers dance
6-10 visitors come and spend 1 Coin each; 2 extra merchants set up stalls
Morale surge: +15 morale, and +10% work speed for the whole next day
Cancelled if a raid is warned; then hold a War Feast instead
nodes.flavor: Tables in the square, pipes in the lane, and nobody works till noon.

nodes.name: Hall of Heroes
nodes.offers: Honour the fallen: memorial plaques, nemesis trophies on the wall, and recruits who arrive braver for it.
details: Every fallen guard gets a memorial plaque with name, rank, kills and the raid they fell in
Trophies of slain nemesis captains hang here: their helmet and banner, with the grudge they held
New recruits who visit the Hall start with +10 morale and courage: they fight on until 30% HP instead of fleeing
'For the fallen!': once per raid, guards fighting in sight of the Hall's banner get +15% damage for 20 s
nodes.flavor: Read their names aloud. Then pick up your spear.

nodes.name: Families & School
nodes.offers: Couples marry, children are born and grow up, and at School they learn a parent's trade with a head start.
details: Couples who share a Townhouse or Manor may marry: a small wedding at the Tavern gives +10 morale village-wide
Children are born when the home has a free bed, grow up over 6 in-game days, and play in the square (visible)
School plan: children attend lessons, then take a parent's trade at trade level 3 (a 2-level head start)
On the alarm, children run to the Keep or their home; they never fight
nodes.flavor: Her father was a smith. She will be a better one.
nodes.change: Reuses the Hall and Learning placeholder id for the School. The Library moves to Scholar's Study, and Kitchen, Dining Hall and Infirmary are split off.

nodes.name: Battle Healers
nodes.offers: Hire Healers at the Infirmary: they bandage the wounded, follow your soldiers into the fight, and are the first answer to permanent death.
details: Healer emblem (3 C, 2 paper, 1 leather), hired at the Infirmary (2 worker slots)
Bandage recipe: Healers and players patch wounds in the field
Healers follow the line in a raid and tend the most wounded soldier nearby; they carry the downed back to the Infirmary
Own Captain's Voice key (H)
nodes.flavor: Hold still. You will live, and you will complain about it.
depends_on: Battle roles lane (being built now; plan/BATTLE-ROLES.md)
Downed state (roadmap phase 3) for carrying the fallen
nodes.change: In code today the Healer and the Infirmary hang off first_raid_aftermath, since hall_and_learning is not implemented.

nodes.name: Cathedral
nodes.offers: A cathedral rises over the town: two Blessings after every victory, and curses bite half as hard.
details: Blessing picks per victory 1 -> 2; legendary Blessings show up twice as often
Curse drawbacks -50%
The bells ring over the town after every victory; on a holy day every 5 days, all settlers get +10 morale
Pick one: Cathedral (Chapel path) or Hall of Revels (Alehouse path)
nodes.flavor: Bells for the living, candles for the fallen.

nodes.name: Hall of Revels
nodes.offers: The greatest hall in the land: Tavern income doubled, travellers flock in, and a Grand Tourney every 4 days.
details: Tavern and guest Coins x2; bard morale x2
Travellers arrive twice as often (more recruits)
Grand Tourney every 4 days: guards spar in the lists for XP, and the winner earns a title shown over their head; all settlers get +20 morale
Pick one: Hall of Revels (Alehouse path) or Cathedral (Chapel path)
nodes.flavor: Ale, song, and a joust at noon.
